Its 2016, and the Promise of the Internet Is Dead

Internet is definitely dead. I am from the old days where web sites and blogs had interesting information.

Now in order to have information I started to use Evernote and Web clipper. Every interesting article I see I automatically let Evernote grab the web page. Then in a later stage I go through every note and remove the formatting. Gets rid of the advertisement and have my content ready for the future if I need it.

I was actually thinking about this last night. I searched for a small, obscure community in Arizona I was curious about, and the only thing I could find was pages and pages of realty sites. I don't suppose we're actually going to start working on any alternatives until one crazy law or another makes it completely useless, though.

This article applies to mainstream users that suck in general at the Internet. They quickly subscribe to bullshit at face value.

Hate to say it but those users would be the same consumers who fell for any historical consumer advertising, too. Sadly, that's a lot of damn people. And this article mostly just shames their appetite for garbage content and shiny products.

In that regard, the article's title should just be "In 2016, If You're Reading This Seriously, You May Be Getting Owned By Corporate Advertising And Propaganda".

The other thing that makes Internet useless are these big footed ugly full screen photos. I mean when I click on a link I expect text no one giant logo on my desktop screen. I expect text that I can read, not a font size so huge that I only see one paragraph at a time and need my mouse to scroll to read the next one.

I don't even bother to read those sites, my automatic reaction is to click the back button.

I don't get it, we are in 2016 and for some dark reasons web site developers lost the ability to scale their font and text for desktop computers.
